title: Your reading list
hookLine: choose ten texts to read in the years ahead
tomorrow: Ông handed Mai his old Dhammapada. how fast should she read it?

cards: Every year-end brings its lists: the songs you played most, the books you finished, the places you went. Here's a harder one.
In this block you've read on your own: the Kalamas, the metta sutta, a chariot, a hare, Guanyin, Vimalakirti, the Pure Land, a poem, a king's stone, a pilgrim, ten pictures.
If you could read only ten more texts, which ten?

teach.b: The Dhammapada has a warning for list-makers. Someone who recites a great deal but doesn't act on it, it says, is, in Max Müller's translation, "like a cowherd counting the cows of others."
A long list of cows you'll never milk. So this list isn't a trophy shelf.
Buddhist teachers name three steps: study, practice, realization. A reading list is only the first.
Build it from what you've met: a Pali sutta you'd read again, a Mahayana text, a story, a poem, a record from history, and room for what you haven't found yet. Ten, not a hundred.
And beside each title, one line: why this one? Then look back, because it's a review day.
Every text this block asked something of you: test a belief, wish all beings safe, sit in silence, hold a name, sit at dusk, name a regret, plan a pilgrimage, find where you are.
A list that remembers those asks is already practice.

how: Buddhist study groups and teachers often suggest a short set of core texts to return to over years, and many practitioners keep one well-worn book, such as the Dhammapada, for daily reading.

o: the full list of every sutta in the Pali canon
ten texts you choose to read and live by in years ahead
a library's list of banned or forbidden scriptures

games.q: about the list — tap the pairs.
p: three steps; a list is the first
the size of the list, not a hundred

s: the Dhammapada praises whoever can recite the most
it compares someone who recites much but doesn't act on it to a cowherd counting the cows of others.
Buddhist teachers name three steps: study, practice and realization
a reading list belongs to the first.

games.q: a friend proudly shows you her list of two hundred books for the year. by today's lesson, what's the kind reply?
o: ask which one she'd most want to live by, and start there
tell her to add more: the longer the list, the deeper she'll go
tell her reading is pointless and only meditation counts
games.why: the Dhammapada warns against counting others' cows: study is a first step toward practice, not a pile to finish.

practice: With a pen, write the first three titles of your ten, and beside each, one line: why this one. Leave the other seven lines blank for now, and sit with the page open in front of you.

wordCard.voice: Your reading list: ten texts chosen for the years ahead, each with a reason, meant to be lived, not counted.

orig.note: Pali: verses of the teaching; the collection quoted today.

carryVoice: Here's the line: ten more, read slowly, each with its reason beside it. List begun.
